deviations.what: every task, every wave and the final PR are additionally reviewed, in parallel, by Qwen Code on the worker role and pi on the associate role, via scripts/dual-review.sh (read-only, throwaway worktree). The plan's merge gate was tests-before-and-after only. Review output is a second opinion: the main agent verifies each finding and records a disposition; a finding it confirms is fixed before merge.
deviations.reason: Operator instruction, 2026-09-21, after merging the archive PR: call Qwen code worker and pi associate (in parallel) to review each task, wave and final PR. Filed against t3 as the first Phase B task; it applies to t3 through t22.

deviations.what: dependency approval record for the realtime redesign: websockets>=15 (base; zero transitive dependencies), sounddevice>=0.5 behind the optional audio extra (cffi, pycparser, system PortAudio), and stdlib http.server for HTTP and SSE. lobes-cli is forbidden as a dependency in any form.
deviations.reason: Operator, 2026-09-21: 'dependencies approved'. Filed because pyproject.toml states every dependency has an approval record in the deviation ledger; this is the planned t3 gate being exercised, not a departure from the plan.

deviations.what: pi (associate) reviews are paused; Qwen Code on the worker role is the sole external reviewer of each task, each wave and the final PR until the operator says otherwise. This amends d1, which named both.
deviations.reason: Operator, 2026-09-22: 'skip pi reviews for now'. Context: across the wave-1 reviews pi returned no usable answer on five large diffs (empty output, 57-60 kB reasoning traces cut off before any answer, one sentence of filler) and no valid finding of its own; causes were diagnosed (pi -p prints only the final text part; the associate model exhausts its output budget reasoning; --thinking levels do not bind for it).

deviations.what: the host audio endpoint (t7) drives the rig's audio through subprocesses the way lobes-cli's realtime-he-accept.py and shabbos-goy do - pw-record/arecord for capture (int16, 16 kHz, 2 channels, channel 1 selected) and pw-play/aplay on plughw for playback (ALSA resamples the 24 kHz TTS) - instead of sounddevice/PortAudio. The sounddevice audio extra approved in d2 is withdrawn; the package keeps zero audio dependencies. Any concrete benefit sounddevice would have had is filed as an improvement issue, not built.
deviations.reason: on the real reSpeaker XVF3800 the sounddevice endpoint never played (OutputStream.write(bytes) TypeError, silent), defaulted output to the HDMI device so the array's AEC had no far-end reference, and needed its own 2:3 resampler for a 16 kHz-only device; both sibling projects that already run this rig use subprocess audio with ALSA's plug layer resampling, and the operator chose to follow them (2026-09-22)

deviations.what: t15 works around eidetic's ASCII-only keyword tokeniser: a lexical recall that returns nothing for an utterance with no ASCII alphanumeric run records app-recall-lexical-blind once and retries the two longest words in exact (substring) mode within the remaining recall deadline; recall.hits_total/rendered_total/lexical_fallback_hits make the path visible. The proper fix is upstream (eidetic-cli issue drafted, unposted); the workaround is pinned by a test on the upstream tokeniser so it is removed when eidetic learns Hebrew.
deviations.reason: Measured 2026-09-22 on the acoustic self-test: eidetic/memory/scoring.py _WORD_RE=[a-z0-9]+ tokenises Hebrew to nothing, so every keyword and hybrid recall Gwen made on this rig returned zero hits with ok=True and no degradation - the remembered fact was stored correctly and never reached a prompt. Verified after the workaround: hits 3, rendered 3, and the reply after a restart carries the fact.

deviations.what: Remembering is a tool the model calls, not a phrase the daemon matches: the turn binds a  tool into the (otherwise empty) registry so  decides when something said is worth keeping and calls it with the fact in its own words; the tool writes to the private store through RoomMemory and is counted (tool calls, records written, refusals). The spoken-phrase detector () stays only as a counted fallback, never the primary path. Recall stays explicit and attributed as before.
deviations.reason: Operator, 2026-09-22 during t21: "We can't have the exact 'תזכרי ש' as key. It needs to be the model calling that tool." Measured in the run: the operator said "remember it all" and the model confirmed while the store wrote nothing (asks_detected 0, ask_not_detected 1) - a phrase key is invisible to the user and wrong for natural speech. Supersedes the t9/t15 decision that v1 ships no tools (the registry gains exactly one).

deviations.what: Remembering is a tool the model calls, not a phrase the daemon matches: the turn binds one remember(fact) tool into the otherwise empty registry, so senses decides when something said is worth keeping and calls it with the fact in its own words; the tool writes to the private store through RoomMemory and is counted (tool calls, records written, refusals). The spoken-phrase detector (the Hebrew "remember that" form) stays only as a counted fallback, never the primary path. Recall stays explicit and attributed as before.
deviations.reason: Restates d6 verbatim - d6 text was mangled by shell quoting when recorded. Operator, 2026-09-22 during t21: "We cannot have the exact phrase as key. It needs to be the model calling that tool." Measured in the run: the operator said "remember it all" and the model confirmed while the store wrote nothing (asks_detected 0, ask_not_detected 1). deviations.what: Decision 18: Gwen gains a forget(record_id) tool that archives a record (eidetic lifecycle archived, excluded from recall), counted like remember; the system prompt forbids claiming to remember or forget unless the tool returned ok; the prompt carries the current local date and time so a recalled record's recorded= timestamp can be related to now. Found in the operator's live session: asked to forget the key location, Gwen said she had, with no tool to do it and the record still active.
deviations.reason: the registry had one tool; a model that claims to forget without a way to is the appearing-attentive failure CLAUDE.md names; recorded= without a clock is unreadable to the model

deviations.what: Decision 19: the daemon's stop budget is re-derived from what stop actually has to do. The runner's shutdown deadline default rises from 2.0 s to 4.0 s, and on stop the session summary runs FIRST, under its own ~2 s share, before the ear and the rest of the close. Measured: at 2.0 s the app's share was 1.6 s and the summary window ~0.24 s, so a live stop recorded session-summary-timeout 1.32 s abandoned and app-shutdown-incomplete: session - the end-of-session memory record was rarely written on a default stop. t21 requires stop under 5 s, which 4.0 s still satisfies.
deviations.reason: the operator's approval, 2026-09-22 ('confirmed all'), on the evidence of the 17:16:55 stop that abandoned its summary

deviations.what: Decision 20: the forget tool accepts the fact's text as well as a record id. When nothing was recalled into the prompt the model has no id to pass, and the live probe showed it refusing with unknown-id on a perfectly ordinary spoken ask. The daemon exact-matches the text against its own private store: exactly one match is archived, no match returns not-found, several return ambiguous - the model never invents an id, and the tool still never deletes a byte.
deviations.reason: the operator's approval, 2026-09-22 ('confirmed all'), on the evidence of the one-sentence forget clip that called the tool and was refused unknown-id
